_meta.description: Industry/role -> expected skill/keyword lookup table (PRD §4). Grows over time as new roles/industries are encountered; populated via reasoning (Claude), not hardcoded permanently.

Head of IT / CIO.skill: 21 CFR Part 11 / GxP computer system validation (CSV)
Head of IT / CIO.why_it_matters: Core regulatory requirement for any validated system in a pharma environment.

Head of IT / CIO.skill: Electronic signature validated state (e.g. DocuSign under Part 11)
Head of IT / CIO.why_it_matters: PRD's own example — common gap between 'used e-signature' and 'maintained validated state through releases'.

Head of IT / CIO.skill: SSO / identity provider specifics (Okta, MS Authenticator, Azure AD)
Head of IT / CIO.why_it_matters: Generic 'IAM' on a resume hides which specific tooling and migrations were actually owned.

Head of IT / CIO.skill: SOX ITGC (IT general controls) and audit readiness
Head of IT / CIO.why_it_matters: Required for public-company or public-company-readiness environments.

Head of IT / CIO.skill: Veeva CRM / Veeva R&D Suite ownership
Head of IT / CIO.why_it_matters: Industry-standard commercial/R&D platform in pharma; depth of ownership vs. peripheral exposure matters.
DSCSA-driven requirement for commercial pharma product launches.

Head of IT / CIO.skill: GxP change control and system lifecycle management
Head of IT / CIO.why_it_matters: Distinguishes 'implemented' from 'implemented and maintained under ongoing change control'.
Resume shows heavy MDM delivery experience — worth confirming ownership of the governance model vs. just implementation.

Head of IT / CIO.skill: Cloud/SaaS vendor governance and cost optimization
Head of IT / CIO.why_it_matters: Resume claims 30% opex reduction — worth probing the specific levers used.

Head of IT / CIO.skill: AI-enabled analytics adoption in a regulated environment
Head of IT / CIO.why_it_matters: Newer area; regulated-industry AI adoption has specific validation/compliance nuances worth capturing in detail.
Resume mentions two SK Life Science integration initiatives — worth capturing what specifically was owned (systems, data, cybersecurity, vendor contracts).

Chief Information Officer (CIO).skill: Regulatory examination readiness for banking supervisors (OCC, FDIC, FRB, FFIEC IT Examination Handbook)
Chief Information Officer (CIO).why_it_matters: Bank and credit union CIOs are directly accountable for evidencing IT control adequacy to examiners, and this is the single most common screening question for the role.

Chief Information Officer (CIO).skill: SOX ITGC ownership plus financial-services control frameworks (COBIT, NIST CSF, ISO 27001)
Chief Information Officer (CIO).why_it_matters: A financial services CIO must own access, change, and operations controls that survive both external audit and internal audit/audit committee scrutiny.

Chief Information Officer (CIO).skill: GLBA Safeguards Rule, FFIEC CAT, and customer data privacy obligations (CCPA/GDPR where applicable)
Chief Information Officer (CIO).why_it_matters: Protecting non-public personal information is a statutory duty for banks, and CIOs are asked how they operationalized it.

Chief Information Officer (CIO).skill: Third-party / vendor risk management under interagency guidance (SOC 2 review, critical-vendor concentration risk, exit planning)
Chief Information Officer (CIO).why_it_matters: Regulators treat outsourced fintech and SaaS providers as an extension of the bank, so vendor governance rigor is evaluated separately from cost savings.

Chief Information Officer (CIO).skill: Core banking platform knowledge (e.g., FIS, Fiserv, Jack Henry, Temenos) and core conversion or modernization experience
Chief Information Officer (CIO).why_it_matters: Core system ownership or conversion leadership is the defining technical credential that distinguishes a banking CIO from a general enterprise CIO.

Chief Information Officer (CIO).skill: Payments and channel infrastructure fluency (ACH/Nacha rules, wires, card networks, real-time payments, digital/online banking platforms)
Chief Information Officer (CIO).why_it_matters: Payments availability and fraud exposure sit at the center of a bank CIO's operational risk portfolio.

Chief Information Officer (CIO).skill: BSA/AML, fraud, and financial crime technology stack oversight (transaction monitoring, sanctions screening, case management)
Chief Information Officer (CIO).why_it_matters: Compliance technology failures create enforcement risk, and the CIO is expected to partner with the BSA officer on platform selection and data quality.

Chief Information Officer (CIO).skill: Business continuity, disaster recovery, and cyber resilience testing with documented RTO/RPO and tabletop exercises
Chief Information Officer (CIO).why_it_matters: Examiners and boards require tested recovery capability for critical banking services, not just documented plans.

Chief Information Officer (CIO).skill: Cybersecurity program leadership: identity and access management, privileged access, endpoint/email security, SOC/MSSP oversight, incident response
Chief Information Officer (CIO).why_it_matters: Financial institutions are prime attack targets and boards expect the CIO to articulate the threat posture and 36-hour incident notification obligations.

Chief Information Officer (CIO).skill: Enterprise data governance, MDM, and analytics for regulatory and risk reporting (customer master, product master, data lineage, BCBS 239-style principles)
Chief Information Officer (CIO).why_it_matters: Accurate, lineage-traceable data is the foundation of credit, liquidity, and regulatory reporting that the CIO is expected to enable.

Chief Information Officer (CIO).skill: Cloud and SaaS strategy in a regulated environment (AWS/Azure landing zones, data residency, cloud concentration risk, contractual audit rights)
Chief Information Officer (CIO).why_it_matters: Banks require cloud adoption to pass regulator and internal audit scrutiny, so the CIO must show governed migration, not just modernization.

Chief Information Officer (CIO).skill: IT budget, capital planning, and P&L discipline with demonstrable run-rate reduction and unit-cost transparency
Chief Information Officer (CIO).why_it_matters: Efficiency ratio pressure makes measurable IT cost management a top hiring criterion for financial services CIOs.

Chief Information Officer (CIO).skill: Board and audit committee reporting, plus CFO/CRO/Chief Compliance Officer partnership
Chief Information Officer (CIO).why_it_matters: CIOs at banks present risk, cyber, and roadmap updates directly to board committees and must translate technology risk into business language.

Chief Information Officer (CIO).skill: M&A technology diligence, Day-1 readiness, and post-close systems/data integration
Chief Information Officer (CIO).why_it_matters: Bank consolidation is constant, and CIOs are frequently hired specifically for their ability to integrate acquired institutions' cores, data, and controls.

Chief Information Officer (CIO).skill: 3-year technology roadmap development with AI/automation strategy and model-risk-aware governance
Chief Information Officer (CIO).why_it_matters: Boards now expect a CIO to present a funded multi-year roadmap that includes AI use cases with clear risk, data, and vendor guardrails.
